questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

But what irked India this time was **(1)**/their attempt to extend the road **(2)**/toward our border. **(3)**/ No Error **(4)**
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the correct preposition here is ‘towards.’ The word ‘toward’ should be replaced here.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Either father or his sons ______ tea.
questions.solution: With words like ‘either or’ the subject to the blank should always considered subject at the end/ second subject thus here the verb should be in plural form because it is followed by "sons" which is plural noun. Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

A small income is preferable ______ no income at all.
questions.solution: The correct preposition here is ‘to’ as ‘preferable’ is always followed with ‘to.’

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

**Root and branch**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09efaba1f03f3617f50d67a80057f02c4fe36af7b8b8c30b73666296abfab598.png] The meaning of the given idiom ‘**root and branch’** means** ‘entirely.’**

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

**White lie**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points __**

 
• The idiom "**white lie**" refers to a** lie that is told with good intentions**, often to spare someone's feelings or avoid hurting them. **It is not meant to harm or deceive someone and is therefore considered a harmless or trivial lie.**
 
• **Option 1) "truth**" is the opposite of a lie and is not the correct meaning of the idiom.
 
• **Option 2) "at large**" refers to something or someone that is still free or not captured, and is completely unrelated to the idiom.
 
• **Option 3) "hidden truth**" is also not the correct meaning of the idiom. While the idiom may involve hiding the truth, it specifically refers to a lie that is told instead of the truth.
 
• Therefore, option 4) "a harmless or trivial lie" is the correct answer that best expresses the meaning of the idiom "white lie."

questions.question:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

They **(are) **also pitched in to help in a major way.
questions.solution: The verb ‘have’ is correct here which is used with a past participle to form the perfect tense.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Indian restaurants **(distributing food)**, Indian businesses are throwing open their premises to provide accommodation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"are distributing food".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The bracketed part does not contain any helping verb. So, it needs improvement.
 
• The verb here must be in Present continuous form as the second part of the sentence is constructed in present continuous form i.e. "are throwing" is used 
 
• The use of "were distributing food" and "should distributing food" is incorrect.
 
• Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence:**__** ***Indian restaurants **__are distributing food__**, Indian businesses are throwing open their premises to provide accommodation.*

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

The Gorkhas

**P: **made their presence felt in

**Q: **India in the 19th century

**R**: battles against the British in
questions.solution: P is the first statement as it mentions the verb which continues the sentence. R cannot be the second statement as ‘in’ is the last word in R. Thus PRQ is the correct order.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Fresh air and clean water are

**P: **life but nothing of both

**Q: **is possible in the modern time

**R: **two most basic needs to sustain
questions.solution: R must be the first statement as it states what they are. P follows R as it mentions what is sustained. Q completes the sentence. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: **Things have become so ______.**

questions.question: writing simple tests and ______
questions.solution: The only word that conveys a proper meaning is ‘completing’ which means ‘finishing’ projects. The word ‘depleting’ means ‘reducing’ and does not fit here.

questions.question: **they tend to ______ the use of books.**
questions.solution: The sentence mentions how the students get used to technology so a negative word should be mentioned here. Thus option 4 is the correct answer. The word ‘memorize’ means ‘commit to memory.’

questions.question: **not have much of a ______ vocabulary.**
questions.solution: The tone of the sentence through the presence of the conjunction ‘but’ makes it clear that the students lack much of a vocabulary. Thus option 2 should fit here. The word ‘ruthless’ means ‘having or showing no pity or compassion for others.’
